From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Spike of 429s this morning — attaching logs

Ben / team / Jordan — quick technical summary from an initial triage:

What we saw
- At ~08:28 PT, the routing layer started returning 429s for requests tied to Acme's tenant ID.
- Our telemetry shows a sudden, brief spike in effective per-API-key token accounting. Two quota records were matched for the tenant due to a recently deployed quota mapping rule: the tenant inherited a global burst-protection cap in addition to their reserved cap. The combination produced a stricter effective cap for some request patterns (particularly long-sequence batch jobs).

Root cause
- A configuration change last night added a general "burst-protection" quota rule with higher precedence than we'd intended. The rule unintentionally matched Acme's tenant because of an overlapping tag filter ("health-" prefix). That produced an intersection of limits, and our enforcement engine applied the more restrictive effective limit which created unexpected 429s for some traffic shapes.

Immediate remediation performed (10:00 PT)
- We rolled back the burst-protection rule that matched the "health-" tag.
- We applied a temporary tenant-specific override to ensure Acme's reserved capacity matched their committed throughput for the next 72 hours.

Next steps (recommended)
- Audit quota mapping rules for tag overlap and add a unit test to prevent higher-precedence rule matches for reserved tenants.
- Add a heuristic to detect when an effective cap drops below a tenant's recent 7-day P99 usage and alert proactively.
- Formal postmortem and customer-facing RCA within 48 hours.

Logs and artifacts:
- Linked a telemetry slice to SERV-1223 (Jira). Full logs and the remediation playbook attached to the internal ticket and shared drive.

I'll prepare a short timeline and suggested wording for the customer update.

Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Action plan and credits — ACME 429 event 2027-05-28

Jordan / team — quick summary for your ops and procurement folks: 

What happened (TL;DR):
- A quota mapping rule deployed last night matched Acme via an overlapping tag filter, producing a temporary effective cap lower than your typical batch peak. That produced a limited window of 429s (08:28–09:04 PT).

What we did: 
- Removed the problematic rule (10:00 PT).
- Applied a temporary override to guarantee your committed throughput for 72 hours.
- We are preparing a longer-term configuration guard and proactive alerting.

Immediate ask from Acme: please confirm whether the temporary override covered the job windows you saw impacted. If you still see residual failures, share a quick reply and we'll escalate to hotfix mode.

Customer-facing remediation / compensation: 
- We will issue a one-time service credit equal to the cost of requests that returned 429s during the incident window. Our CS team will calculate the amount and send a credit memo within 5 business days.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem (internal + customer RCA) to be shared by 2027-05-30 17:00 PT.
- Engineering changes to quota mapping and tests targeted for the next sprint (SERV-1223).

Thanks again for the heads-up. Sorry for the disruption — we take this seriously and will follow through.

Best,
Ben Carter
